499	  /**
500	   *
501	   * @param {Object} payload - old book object
502	   * @returns {Promise<boolean>}
503	   */
504	  async updateFromRequest(payload: BookUpdatePayload) {
505	    if (!payload) return false
506	
507	    let hasUpdates = false
508	
509	    if (payload.metadata) {
510	      const metadataStringKeys: MetadataStringKey[] = ['title', 'subtitle', 'publishedYear', 'publishedDate', 'publisher', 'description', 'isbn', 'asin', 'language']
511	      metadataStringKeys.forEach((key) => {
512	        if (typeof payload.metadata[key] == 'number') {
513	          payload.metadata[key] = String(payload.metadata[key])
514	        }
515	
516	        if ((typeof payload.metadata[key] === 'string' || payload.metadata[key] === null) && this[key] !== payload.metadata[key]) {
517	          // Sanitize description HTML
518	          if (key === 'description' && payload.metadata[key]) {
519	            const sanitizedDescription = htmlSanitizer.sanitize(payload.metadata[key])
520	            if (sanitizedDescription !== payload.metadata[key]) {
521	              Logger.debug(`[Book] "${this.title}" Sanitized description from "${payload.metadata[key]}" to "${sanitizedDescription}"`)
522	              payload.metadata[key] = sanitizedDescription
523	            }
524	          }
525	
526	          this[key] = payload.metadata[key] || null
527	
528	          if (key === 'title') {
529	            this.titleIgnorePrefix = getTitleIgnorePrefix(this.title)
530	          }
531	
532	          hasUpdates = true
533	        }
534	      })
535	      if (payload.metadata.explicit !== undefined && this.explicit !== !!payload.metadata.explicit) {
536	        this.explicit = !!payload.metadata.explicit
537	        hasUpdates = true
538	      }
539	      if (payload.metadata.abridged !== undefined && this.abridged !== !!payload.metadata.abridged) {
540	        this.abridged = !!payload.metadata.abridged
541	        hasUpdates = true
542	      }
543	      const arrayOfStringsKeys: ('narrators' | 'genres')[] = ['narrators', 'genres']
544	      arrayOfStringsKeys.forEach((key) => {
545	        if (Array.isArray(payload.metadata[key]) && !payload.metadata[key].some((item) => typeof item !== 'string') && JSON.stringify(this[key]) !== JSON.stringify(payload.metadata[key])) {
546	          this[key] = payload.metadata[key]
547	          this.changed(key, true)
548	          hasUpdates = true
549	        }
550	      })
551	    }
552	
553	    if (Array.isArray(payload.tags) && !payload.tags.some((tag) => typeof tag !== 'string') && JSON.stringify(this.tags) !== JSON.stringify(payload.tags)) {
554	      this.tags = payload.tags
555	      this.changed('tags', true)
556	      hasUpdates = true
557	    }
558	
559	    if (hasUpdates) {
560	      Logger.debug(`[Book] "${this.title}" changed keys:`, this.changed())
561	      await this.save()
562	    }
563	
564	    return hasUpdates
565	  }

568	   * Creates or removes authors from the book using the author names from the request
569	   *
570	   * @param {string[]} authors
571	   * @param {string} libraryId
572	   * @returns {Promise<{authorsRemoved: import('./Author')[], authorsAdded: import('./Author')[]}>}
573	   */
574	  async updateAuthorsFromRequest(authors: string[], libraryId: string) {
575	    if (!Array.isArray(authors)) return null
576	
577	    if (!this.authors) {
578	      throw new Error(`[Book] Cannot update authors because authors are not loaded for book ${this.id}`)
579	    }
580	
581	    /** @type {typeof import('./Author')} */
582	    const authorModel = this.sequelize.models.author
583	
584	    /** @type {typeof import('./BookAuthor')} */
585	    const bookAuthorModel = this.sequelize.models.bookAuthor
586	
587	    const authorsCleaned = authors.map((a) => a.toLowerCase()).filter((a) => a)
588	    const authorsRemoved = this.authors.filter((au) => !authorsCleaned.includes(au.name.toLowerCase()))
589	    const newAuthorNames = authors.filter((a) => !this.authors.some((au) => au.name.toLowerCase() === a.toLowerCase()))
590	
591	    for (const author of authorsRemoved) {
592	      await bookAuthorModel.removeByIds(author.id, this.id)
593	      const numBooks = await bookAuthorModel.getCountForAuthor(author.id)
594	      if (numBooks > 0) {
595	        SocketAuthority.emitter('author_updated', author.toOldJSONExpanded(numBooks))
596	      }
597	      Logger.debug(`[Book] "${this.title}" Removed author "${author.name}"`)
598	      this.authors = this.authors.filter((au) => au.id !== author.id)
599	    }
600	    const authorsAdded: Author[] = []
601	    for (const authorName of newAuthorNames) {
602	      const { author, created } = await authorModel.findOrCreateByNameAndLibrary(authorName, libraryId)
603	      await bookAuthorModel.create({ bookId: this.id, authorId: author.id })
604	      if (created) {
605	        SocketAuthority.emitter('author_added', author.toOldJSON())
606	      } else {
607	        const numBooks = await bookAuthorModel.getCountForAuthor(author.id)
608	        SocketAuthority.emitter('author_updated', author.toOldJSONExpanded(numBooks))
609	      }
610	      Logger.debug(`[Book] "${this.title}" Added author "${author.name}"`)
611	      this.authors.push(author)
612	      authorsAdded.push(author)
613	    }
614	
615	    return {
616	      authorsRemoved,
617	      authorsAdded
618	    }
619	  }

621	  /**
622	   * Creates or removes series from the book using the series names from the request.
623	   * Updates series sequence if it has changed.
624	   *
625	   * @param {{ name: string, sequence: string }[]} seriesObjects
626	   * @param {string} libraryId
627	   * @returns {Promise<{seriesRemoved: import('./Series')[], seriesAdded: import('./Series')[], hasUpdates: boolean}>}
628	   */
629	  async updateSeriesFromRequest(seriesObjects: { name: string; sequence?: string | null }[], libraryId: string) {
630	    if (!Array.isArray(seriesObjects) || seriesObjects.some((se) => !se.name || typeof se.name !== 'string')) return null
631	
632	    if (!this.series) {
633	      throw new Error(`[Book] Cannot update series because series are not loaded for book ${this.id}`)
634	    }
635	
636	    /** @type {typeof import('./Series')} */
637	    const seriesModel = this.sequelize.models.series
638	
639	    /** @type {typeof import('./BookSeries')} */
640	    const bookSeriesModel = this.sequelize.models.bookSeries
641	
642	    const seriesNamesCleaned = seriesObjects.map((se) => se.name.toLowerCase())
643	    const seriesRemoved = this.series.filter((se) => !seriesNamesCleaned.includes(se.name.toLowerCase()))
644	    const seriesAdded: SeriesExpanded[] = []
645	    let hasUpdates = false
646	    for (const seriesObj of seriesObjects) {
647	      const seriesObjSequence = typeof seriesObj.sequence === 'string' ? seriesObj.sequence : null
648	
649	      const existingSeries = this.series.find((se) => se.name.toLowerCase() === seriesObj.name.toLowerCase())
650	      if (existingSeries) {
651	        if (existingSeries.bookSeries.sequence !== seriesObjSequence) {
652	          existingSeries.bookSeries.sequence = seriesObjSequence
653	          await existingSeries.bookSeries.save()
654	          hasUpdates = true
655	          Logger.debug(`[Book] "${this.title}" Updated series "${existingSeries.name}" sequence ${seriesObjSequence}`)
656	        }
657	      } else {
658	        const series = await seriesModel.findOrCreateByNameAndLibrary(seriesObj.name, libraryId)
659	        series.bookSeries = await bookSeriesModel.create({ bookId: this.id, seriesId: series.id, sequence: seriesObjSequence })
660	        this.series.push(series)
661	        seriesAdded.push(series)
662	        hasUpdates = true
663	        Logger.debug(`[Book] "${this.title}" Added series "${series.name}"`)
664	      }
665	    }
666	
667	    for (const series of seriesRemoved) {
668	      await bookSeriesModel.removeByIds(series.id, this.id)
669	      this.series = this.series.filter((se) => se.id !== series.id)
670	      Logger.debug(`[Book] "${this.title}" Removed series ${series.id}`)
671	      hasUpdates = true
672	    }
673	
674	    return {
675	      seriesRemoved,
676	      seriesAdded,
677	      hasUpdates
678	    }
679	  }

# PO-S07: the 8 skipped models, bug fixes allowed (one agent, test first)

Date: 2026-10-10 (NZDT). Branch Aung-Min-Myat/po-s01. Stage base: 33931ea9 (PO-S05 evidence commit).
Planned settings: Opus 5.5, max effort, auto mode (set in the session by the user, as in PO-S05). Cap: 150 minutes after the agent's start.

## Starting state (evidence/test-results/PO-S07/preflight.txt)
- server/models: 17 .ts and 8 .js (Author 208 lines, Collection 292, Feed 682, FeedEpisode 349, LibraryItem 1044, PlaybackSession 257, Playlist 379, User 1026).
- Clean build: 0 "error TS", 356 passing, 0 failing, 464 files in dist-server. Copy saved in D:\SEM-2\574\Project\po-s07-baseline.
- No test file loads any of the 8 models by file path (search pattern: models/<Name>). They may be reached through Database, so this is not proof of zero coverage.
- Permission rules before the run: .claude/settings.local.json denied Edit(test/**). It was replaced by one deny rule per existing test folder, so that only the new folder test/server/bugfix/ can receive files (settings.local.before.json and settings.local.after.json in the evidence folder). These rules cover the edit tools only; shell commands that write files are not covered. After the run we check with git that no existing test file changed.

## What this run changes compared with PO-S05
1. One agent, one model at a time, no sub-agents (PO-S05: a main agent and four sub-agents in two waves).
2. Rule 1 (type-only, no bug fixes) is relaxed in two ways: bug fixes with a test written first, and behaviour-preserving edits that the types need.
3. Rule 5 is read strictly (a cast only on an untyped module, ! only on a field that starts as null). In PO-S05 the main agent chose a wider reading for BookAuthor and MediaProgress.
4. New test files are allowed in test/server/bugfix/ only.
5. Each step is built, tested and committed alone (PO-S05: four commits after one run).
6. CLAUDE.md is unchanged. The prompt states the exceptions. The 17 converted models are named as the worked examples.
Changed variables are therefore: the permission to fix bugs, the strict reading of rule 5, the one-agent serial structure, and the existence of 14 more converted examples. The results cannot be credited to one of them alone.

## Measurements planned
- /usage before and after (usage-start.txt, usage-end.txt) and the end-of-run cost. Taken before the 5-hour reset this time.
- Checkpoints every 15 minutes in run-log.txt. Prompts answered by the user and the "Recently denied" list are recorded at the end.
- After the run: scope and protected paths, banned tokens, every bug fix checked independently (the new test fails on the parent commit and passes on the fix commit), a build and test run of every commit alone, a compiled-output comparison for each conversion commit, five clean builds at the end.

624

626	    const mediaExpanded = this.media || (await this.getMediaExpanded())
627	
628	    let jsonObject = {}
629	    if (this.mediaType === 'book') {
630	      jsonObject = {
631	        tags: mediaExpanded.tags || [],

633	        title: mediaExpanded.title,

639	          if (!sequence) return se.name
640	          return `${se.name} #${sequence}`
641	        }),
642	        genres: mediaExpanded.genres || [],
643	        publishedYear: mediaExpanded.publishedYear,
644	        publishedDate: mediaExpanded.publishedDate,
645	        publisher: mediaExpanded.publisher,

650	        explicit: !!mediaExpanded.explicit,
651	        abridged: !!mediaExpanded.abridged
652	      }
653	    } else {
654	      jsonObject = {
655	        tags: mediaExpanded.tags || [],
656	        title: mediaExpanded.title,
657	        author: mediaExpanded.author,
658	        description: mediaExpanded.description,
659	        releaseDate: mediaExpanded.releaseDate,

729	   */
730	  async createUpdateMediaProgressFromPayload(progressPayload) {
731	    /** @type {import('./MediaProgress')|null} */
732	    let mediaProgress = null
733	    let mediaItemId = null
734	    let podcastId = null
735	    if (progressPayload.episodeId) {
736	      const podcastEpisode = await this.sequelize.models.podcastEpisode.findByPk(progressPayload.episodeId, {
737	        attributes: ['id', 'podcastId'],
738	        include: [
739	          {
740	            model: this.sequelize.models.mediaProgress,
741	            where: { userId: this.id },
742	            required: false
743	          },
744	          {
745	            model: this.sequelize.models.podcast,
746	            attributes: ['id', 'title'],
747	            include: {
748	              model: this.sequelize.models.libraryItem,
749	              attributes: ['id']
750	            }
751	          }
752	        ]
753	      })
754	      if (!podcastEpisode) {
755	        Logger.error(`[User] createUpdateMediaProgress: episode ${progressPayload.episodeId} not found`)
756	        return {
757	          error: 'Episode not found',
758	          statusCode: 404
759	        }
760	      }
761	      mediaItemId = podcastEpisode.id
762	      mediaProgress = podcastEpisode.mediaProgresses?.[0]
763	      podcastId = podcastEpisode.podcastId
764	    } else {
765	      const libraryItem = await this.sequelize.models.libraryItem.findByPk(progressPayload.libraryItemId, {
766	        attributes: ['id', 'mediaId', 'mediaType'],
767	        include: {
768	          model: this.sequelize.models.book,
769	          attributes: ['id', 'title'],
770	          required: false,
771	          include: {
772	            model: this.sequelize.models.mediaProgress,
773	            where: { userId: this.id },
774	            required: false
775	          }
776	        }
777	      })
778	      if (!libraryItem) {
779	        Logger.error(`[User] createUpdateMediaProgress: library item ${progressPayload.libraryItemId} not found`)
780	        return {
781	          error: 'Library item not found',
782	          statusCode: 404
783	        }
784	      } else if (libraryItem.mediaType !== 'book') {
785	        Logger.error(`[User] createUpdateMediaProgress: library item ${progressPayload.libraryItemId} is not a book`)
786	        return {
787	          error: 'Library item is not a book',
788	          statusCode: 400
789	        }
790	      }
791	
792	      mediaItemId = libraryItem.media.id
793	      mediaProgress = libraryItem.media.mediaProgresses?.[0]
794	    }
795	
796	    if (mediaProgress) {
797	      mediaProgress = await mediaProgress.applyProgressUpdate(progressPayload)
798	      this.mediaProgresses = this.mediaProgresses.map((mp) => (mp.id === mediaProgress.id ? mediaProgress : mp))
799	    } else {
800	      const newMediaProgressPayload = {
801	        userId: this.id,
802	        mediaItemId,
803	        podcastId,
804	        mediaItemType: progressPayload.episodeId ? 'podcastEpisode' : 'book',
805	        duration: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.duration) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.duration),
806	        currentTime: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.currentTime) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.currentTime),
807	        isFinished: !!progressPayload.isFinished,
808	        hideFromContinueListening: !!progressPayload.hideFromContinueListening,
809	        ebookLocation: progressPayload.ebookLocation || null,
810	        ebookProgress: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.ebookProgress) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.ebookProgress),
811	        finishedAt: progressPayload.finishedAt || null,
812	        createdAt: progressPayload.createdAt || new Date(),
813	        extraData: {
814	          libraryItemId: progressPayload.libraryItemId,
815	          progress: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.progress) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.progress)
816	        }
817	      }
818	      if (newMediaProgressPayload.isFinished) {
819	        newMediaProgressPayload.finishedAt = newMediaProgressPayload.finishedAt || new Date()
820	        newMediaProgressPayload.extraData.progress = 1
821	      } else {
822	        newMediaProgressPayload.finishedAt = null
823	      }
824	      mediaProgress = await this.sequelize.models.mediaProgress.create(newMediaProgressPayload)
825	      this.mediaProgresses.push(mediaProgress)
826	    }
827	    userCache.maybeInvalidate(this)
828	    return {
829	      mediaProgress
830	    }
831	  }

947	  /**
948	   * Update user permissions from external JSON
949	   *
950	   * @param {Object} absPermissions JSON containing user permissions
951	   * @returns {Promise<boolean>} true if updates were made
952	   */
953	  async updatePermissionsFromExternalJSON(absPermissions) {
954	    if (!this.permissions) this.permissions = {}
955	    let hasUpdates = false
956	
957	    // Map the boolean permissions from absPermissions
958	    Object.keys(absPermissions).forEach((absKey) => {
959	      const userPermKey = User.permissionMapping[absKey]
960	      if (!userPermKey) {
961	        throw new Error(`Unexpected permission property: ${absKey}`)
962	      }
963	
964	      if (!['librariesAccessible', 'itemTagsSelected'].includes(userPermKey)) {
965	        if (this.permissions[userPermKey] !== !!absPermissions[absKey]) {
966	          this.permissions[userPermKey] = !!absPermissions[absKey]
967	          hasUpdates = true
968	        }
969	      }
970	    })
971	
972	    // Handle allowedLibraries
973	    const librariesAccessible = this.permissions.librariesAccessible || []
974	    if (this.permissions.accessAllLibraries) {
975	      if (librariesAccessible.length) {
976	        this.permissions.librariesAccessible = []
977	        hasUpdates = true
978	      }
979	    } else if (absPermissions.allowedLibraries?.length && absPermissions.allowedLibraries.join(',') !== librariesAccessible.join(',')) {
980	      if (absPermissions.allowedLibraries.some((lid) => typeof lid !== 'string')) {
981	        throw new Error('Invalid permission property "allowedLibraries", expecting array of strings')
982	      }
983	      this.permissions.librariesAccessible = absPermissions.allowedLibraries
984	      hasUpdates = true
985	    }
986	
987	    // Handle allowedTags
988	    const itemTagsSelected = this.permissions.itemTagsSelected || []
989	    if (this.permissions.accessAllTags) {
990	      if (itemTagsSelected.length) {
991	        this.permissions.itemTagsSelected = []
992	        hasUpdates = true
993	      }
994	    } else if (absPermissions.allowedTags?.length && absPermissions.allowedTags.join(',') !== itemTagsSelected.join(',')) {
995	      if (absPermissions.allowedTags.some((tag) => typeof tag !== 'string')) {

### Escape hatches, with reasons

**Author.ts** (all in `getAllLibraryItemsForAuthor`)
- 116 `if (author!.books) {`: `findByPk()` returns `Author | null`; the original dereferences it unchecked.
- 117 `for (const book of author!.books) {`: same.
- 118 `const libraryItem = book.libraryItem!`: set by the include. It is optional in my type only because line 120 does `delete book.libraryItem`, which TS2790 allows only on an optional property.

**PlaybackSession.ts**
- 100 `} as FindOptions)`: `getOldPlaybackSessions(where = null)` passes `where: null` to `findAll`. `FindOptions.where` does not allow null. The shorthand `where,` leaves no narrower place for a cast without changing emitted text.
- 159 `} as UpsertOptions)`: `{ silent: true }` is passed to `upsert`, and `UpsertOptions` has no `silent` key (excess-property error).

**Podcast.ts**
- 29 `metadata: { [key: string]: unknown }` and 30 `[key: string]: unknown`, both in the erased `PodcastRequestPayload` interface: `payload.metadata[key]` and `payload[key]` are read and written by dynamic key.
- 67 class index signature `[key: string]: unknown`: `updateFromRequest()` does `this[newKey] = ...` and `this[key] = ...`. This makes any unknown property on a Podcast instance `unknown` instead of an error, which may change how errors look in LibraryItem.ts for `Book | Podcast` unions.

Not counted above: `Record<string, unknown>` for JSON columns whose JSDoc says `Object` and whose keys the file never reads (MediaItemShare `extraData`, PlaybackSession `mediaMetadata`).

Lines whose trailing comments will show in compiled JS: Author.ts 116, 117, 118 and PlaybackSession.ts 100, 159. Everything else I added sits on erased lines.

unknown author id rejects with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'books')".

- "returns the library items of a known author" is a control for the normal path. It
  passes before and after.

Fix: if (author?.books). The method is documented to return an array of library items
and already returns [] when the author has no books, so an unknown author gives [].

Build passes. npm test: 358 passing (356 + 2 new), 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Collection: fix the permission filter of getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded being stored on the class (test added)

Reported bug (Collection.js:99): this.books = books is inside a static method, so the
permission-filtered list is assigned to the Collection class. c.toOldJSONExpanded()
still reads the unfiltered c.books, so a restricted user gets every book of a
collection as soon as one book is accessible.

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Collection.getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded.test.js
(3 tests). A collection holds one clean and one explicit book.
- "leaves out the books that the user is not allowed to access" fails on the unfixed
  code: a user without explicit-content access gets both books.
- "does not store the filtered books on the Collection class" fails on the unfixed
  code: the class has an own property books after the call.
- "returns every book of the collection to a user who can access explicit content" is
  a control. It passes before and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Collection-static-this-books-before.txt
(1 passing, 2 failing) and Collection-static-this-books-after.txt (3 passing).

Fix: c.books = books. The instance method getOldJsonExpanded() does the same filter
and assigns the result to this.books of the collection, which shows the intent.

Build passes. npm test: 361 passing (356 + 5 new), 0 failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[PO-S07] FeedEpisode: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only, plus three edits of point 1(b). The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 0 index signatures, 1 cast, 0 declare sequelize lines.
- Cast (allowed: untyped module): const date = dateAndTime as typeof dateAndTime &
  { format(dateObj: Date, formatString: string): string }. The minified
  libs/dateAndTime is inferred without format(). Same line as in objects/DailyLog.ts.

Point 1(b) edits. How I know the behaviour is the same: the compiled file differs
from the compiled file of the previous commit only in the require lines and in the
lines listed here, and each line is equivalent for the reason given.
1. createFromPodcastEpisodes(), two sort callbacks:
   new Date(b.pubDate) - new Date(a.pubDate)
   -> new Date(b.pubDate).getTime() - new Date(a.pubDate).getTime()
   Needed: TS2362/TS2363 (Date operands). Same: the - operator converts a Date with
   valueOf(), which returns what getTime() returns (NaN for an invalid date in both).
2. checkUseChapterTitlesForEpisodes() and getFeedEpisodeObjFromAudiobookTrack():
   chapters[i].start - trackList[i].startOffset
   -> chapters[i].start - Number(trackList[i].startOffset)   (and the same for
   ch.start - audioTrack.startOffset)
   Needed: Book.getTracklist() returns startOffset as optional (Book.ts, PO-S05), and
   number | undefined is not allowed in a subtraction. Same: the - operator applies
   ToNumber to its operand, which is what Number() does, for every non-BigInt value.
3. createFromBooks(), first line of the loop over books:
   if (earliestLibraryItemCreatedAt === null) break
   Needed: the local is Date | null and getFeedEpisodeObjFromAudiobookTrack() takes a
   Date; no ! is allowed here. Same: the value is null only when books.length > 0 is
   false, and then the loop body does not run, so the line is never taken. This is
   the least obvious of the three edits: it is an added guard, not a rewritten
   expression.

Types: season, episode and episodeType are string | null (not set for an audiobook
track). The track parameters use the return type of Book.getTracklist(). The two
create functions for a library item take LibraryItemExpanded with media narrowed to
PodcastExpanded or BookExpanded. getRSSData() types its custom elements as a union of
single-key objects (no index signature).

Build passes. npm test: 358 passing, 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Collection: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only, plus two edits of point 1(b). The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 0 index signatures, 0 casts, 1 declare sequelize line
(declare static readonly sequelize: sequelizeModule.Sequelize; written with the module
name because Sequelize is a runtime value in this file).

Point 1(b) edits:
1. getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded():
   where: collectionWhere  ->  ...(collectionWhere && { where: collectionWhere })
   Needed: collectionWhere is null when no libraryId is given, and the typings of
   Sequelize reject where: null (TS2322). Same behaviour: Sequelize builds no WHERE
   clause for a null where (whereItemsQuery returns '' for null) and none when the key
   is missing. Checked by running the query before and after with SQL logging: the
   SQL text is identical with and without a libraryId. The three tests of
   Collection.getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded.test.js pass.
2. toOldJSONExpanded():
   delete book.libraryItem
   -> const bookWithOptionalItem: { libraryItem?: LibraryItem } = book
      delete bookWithOptionalItem.libraryItem
   Needed: the line above reads book.libraryItem with no guard, so the property must
   be required, and TypeScript only allows delete on an optional property (TS2790).
   Same behaviour: the alias is the same object and the same delete operator runs.
   (Same edit as in Author.ts.)
The compiled file differs from the compiled file of the previous commit only in the

[PO-S07] Collection: fix the permission filter of getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded being stored on the class (test added)

Reported bug (Collection.js:99): this.books = books is inside a static method, so the
permission-filtered list is assigned to the Collection class. c.toOldJSONExpanded()
still reads the unfiltered c.books, so a restricted user gets every book of a
collection as soon as one book is accessible.

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Collection.getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded.test.js
(3 tests). A collection holds one clean and one explicit book.
- "leaves out the books that the user is not allowed to access" fails on the unfixed
  code: a user without explicit-content access gets both books.
- "does not store the filtered books on the Collection class" fails on the unfixed
  code: the class has an own property books after the call.
- "returns every book of the collection to a user who can access explicit content" is
  a control. It passes before and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Collection-static-this-books-before.txt
(1 passing, 2 failing) and Collection-static-this-books-after.txt (3 passing).

Fix: c.books = books. The instance method getOldJsonExpanded() does the same filter
and assigns the result to this.books of the collection, which shows the intent.

Build passes. npm test: 361 passing (356 + 5 new), 0 failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

import sequelizeModule = require('sequelize')
const { DataTypes, Model } = sequelizeModule
import type { BelongsToGetAssociationMixin, BelongsToGetAssociationMixinOptions, BuildOptions, CreationAttributes, Sequelize, WhereOptions } from 'sequelize'

import oldPlaybackSession = require('../objects/PlaybackSession')

type Book = import('./Book')
type PodcastEpisode = import('./PodcastEpisode')
type Device = import('./Device')

class PlaybackSession extends Model {
  declare id: string
  declare mediaItemId: string
  declare mediaItemType: 'book' | 'podcastEpisode' // the JSDoc says string; these are the two values getFromOld() stores and the associations in init() are scoped to, and getMediaItem() builds a mixin name from them
  declare displayTitle: string
  declare displayAuthor: string
  declare duration: number
  declare playMethod: number
  declare mediaPlayer: string
  declare startTime: number
  declare currentTime: number
  declare serverVersion: string | null // getFromOld() stores null when the old session has no version; the JSDoc says string
  declare coverPath: string
  declare timeListening: number
  declare mediaMetadata: Record<string, unknown>
  declare date: string
  declare dayOfWeek: string

throws "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')".

asks for a book (the JSDoc: "Old model used libraryItemId instead of bookId"), and a
podcast-episode item is not that book, so it does not match.

an episode of that podcast. The fix returns false for it. The one caller
(PlaylistController.addItem) rejects that input before it calls the method.

[PO-S07] Playlist: fix the re-order update of removeMediaItemsFromPlaylists not being awaited (test added)

Reported bug (Playlist.js:190): playlistMediaItem.update({ order }) is called without
await inside an async loop. The method goes on, builds the playlist JSON and emits
playlist_updated (or destroys the playlist) while the saves are still running, and a
failed save becomes an unhandled rejection instead of an error of the method.

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Playlist.removeMediaItemsFromPlaylists.test.js
(2 tests). A playlist holds three books and the first one is removed.
- "waits until the new order of each remaining item is saved before it reports the
  playlist" slows the save of the order by 50 ms (a sinon stub that calls the real
  update) and records the order of events. On the unfixed code the event list is
  ['playlist_updated'] when the method returns; after the fix it is
  ['order saved', 'order saved', 'playlist_updated'].
- "removes the media item and renumbers the remaining items" is a control on the
  final rows. It passes before and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Playlist-update-not-awaited-before.txt
(1 passing, 1 failing) and Playlist-update-not-awaited-after.txt (2 passing).

Fix: await playlistMediaItem.update({ order }). The destroy() in the other branch of
the same loop is awaited, which shows the intent.

Build passes. npm test: 366 passing (356 + 10 new), 0 failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[PO-S07] Playlist: fix checkHasMediaItem throwing for a podcast-episode item when no episodeId is given (test added)

Reported bug (Playlist.js:332): without an episodeId the method reads
pmi.mediaItem.libraryItem.id for every item. A podcast-episode item has its library
item under mediaItem.podcast, so mediaItem.libraryItem is undefined and the call
throws "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')".

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Playlist.checkHasMediaItem.test.js (3 tests). The
playlists are loaded as PlaylistController.addItem loads them.
- "returns false for a book when the playlist holds a podcast episode" fails on the
  unfixed code and passes after the fix.
- "finds a book by its library item id" and "finds a podcast episode by its episode
  id" are controls. They pass before and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Playlist-checkHasMediaItem-episode-before.txt
(2 passing, 1 failing) and Playlist-checkHasMediaItem-episode-after.txt (3 passing).

Fix: pmi.mediaItem.libraryItem?.id === libraryItemId. Without an episodeId the caller
asks for a book (the JSDoc: "Old model used libraryItemId instead of bookId"), and a
podcast-episode item is not that book, so it does not match.
Not decided here: whether a podcast library item id without an episodeId should match
an episode of that podcast. The fix returns false for it. The one caller
(PlaylistController.addItem) rejects that input before it calls the method.

Build passes. npm test: 364 passing (356 + 8 new), 0 failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[PO-S07] Playlist: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only, plus edits of point 1(b) of two kinds. The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 0 index signatures, 0 casts, 1 declare sequelize line
(declare static readonly sequelize: Sequelize & { models: RegisteredModels }, with
the one entry playlistMediaItem, as in MediaItemShare.ts).

Point 1(b) edits:
1. A nested include given as an array, in seven places of three queries
   (getOldPlaylistsForUserAndLibrary: 2, getPlaylistsForMediaItemIds: 4,
   getMediaItemsExpandedWithLibraryItem: 1). For example:
   include: { model: podcast, include: libraryItem }
   -> include: [{ model: podcast, include: [libraryItem] }]
   Needed: IncludeOptions.include only takes an array (TS2322/TS2353); only the
   top-level include of a query may be a single object. Same behaviour: Sequelize
   wraps a single include in an array itself (Model._conformIncludes, at every
   level). Checked by running the three queries before and after with SQL logging:
   the SQL text is identical.
2. toOldJSONExpanded(), two places:
   delete pmi.mediaItem.libraryItem
   -> const bookWithOptionalItem: { libraryItem?: LibraryItem } = pmi.mediaItem
      delete bookWithOptionalItem.libraryItem
   (and the same for pmi.mediaItem.podcast.libraryItem)
   Needed: the line above reads the property with no guard, so it must be required,
   and TypeScript only allows delete on an optional property (TS2790). Same
   behaviour: the alias is the same object and the same delete operator runs.
   (Same edit as in Author.ts and Collection.ts.)
The compiled file differs from the compiled file of the previous commit only in the
require lines and in these lines (compared with diff -w, because the wrapped includes
are indented deeper). The five Playlist tests of the two previous commits pass; they
run both rewritten parts.

Types: playlistMediaItems is a union of two shapes that mediaItemType tells apart
(a book with its library item, or a podcast episode whose podcast has the library
item), so the tests of mediaItemType in the hook, in getPlaylistsForMediaItemIds()
and in toOldJSONExpanded() narrow mediaItem. toOldJSON() has an explicit return type
with an optional items key.

Build passes. npm test: 366 passing, 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Playlist: fix the re-order update of removeMediaItemsFromPlaylists not being awaited (test added)

Reported bug (Playlist.js:190): playlistMediaItem.update({ order }) is called without
await inside an async loop. The method goes on, builds the playlist JSON and emits
playlist_updated (or destroys the playlist) while the saves are still running, and a
failed save becomes an unhandled rejection instead of an error of the method.

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Playlist.removeMediaItemsFromPlaylists.test.js
(2 tests). A playlist holds three books and the first one is removed.
- "waits until the new order of each remaining item is saved before it reports the
  playlist" slows the save of the order by 50 ms (a sinon stub that calls the real
  update) and records the order of events. On the unfixed code the event list is
  ['playlist_updated'] when the method returns; after the fix it is
  ['order saved', 'order saved', 'playlist_updated'].
- "removes the media item and renumbers the remaining items" is a control on the
  final rows. It passes before and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Playlist-update-not-awaited-before.txt
(1 passing, 1 failing) and Playlist-update-not-awaited-after.txt (2 passing).

Fix: await playlistMediaItem.update({ order }). The destroy() in the other branch of
the same loop is awaited, which shows the intent.

Build passes. npm test: 366 passing (356 + 10 new), 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Feed: fix updateFeedForEntity throwing when the entity of the feed no longer exists (test added)

Reported bug (Feed.js:511, also 489 and 502): the result of getExpandedById() is
passed on with no null check. When the library item, collection or series of a feed
is gone, the method rejects with a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of null (reading
'media')" or "(reading 'books')"). The three places are before the try block, so the
catch that returns null does not apply.

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Feed.updateFeedForEntity.test.js (4 tests).
- "returns null when the library item / the collection / the series of the feed no
  longer exists" (3 tests) fail on the unfixed code and pass after the fix.
- "updates the feed of an existing series" is a control for the normal path. It
  passes before and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Feed-missing-entity-before.txt (1 passing,
3 failing) and Feed-missing-entity-after.txt (4 passing).

Fix: in each of the three branches, if the entity is not found, Logger.error and
return null. This is what the method already does for its two other failures (an
invalid entity type, and an error inside the transaction).

Not fixed, only reported: the caller RssFeedManager.getFeed() calls feed.buildXml()
on the result without a null check, for all of these null returns.

Build passes. npm test: 370 passing (356 + 14 new), 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Playlist: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only, plus edits of point 1(b) of two kinds. The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 0 index signatures, 0 casts, 1 declare sequelize line
(declare static readonly sequelize: Sequelize & { models: RegisteredModels }, with
the one entry playlistMediaItem, as in MediaItemShare.ts).

Point 1(b) edits:
1. A nested include given as an array, in seven places of three queries
   (getOldPlaylistsForUserAndLibrary: 2, getPlaylistsForMediaItemIds: 4,
   getMediaItemsExpandedWithLibraryItem: 1). For example:
   include: { model: podcast, include: libraryItem }
   -> include: [{ model: podcast, include: [libraryItem] }]
   Needed: IncludeOptions.include only takes an array (TS2322/TS2353); only the
   top-level include of a query may be a single object. Same behaviour: Sequelize
   wraps a single include in an array itself (Model._conformIncludes, at every
   level). Checked by running the three queries before and after with SQL logging:
   the SQL text is identical.
2. toOldJSONExpanded(), two places:
   delete pmi.mediaItem.libraryItem
   -> const bookWithOptionalItem: { libraryItem?: LibraryItem } = pmi.mediaItem
      delete bookWithOptionalItem.libraryItem
   (and the same for pmi.mediaItem.podcast.libraryItem)
   Needed: the line above reads the property with no guard, so it must be required,
   and TypeScript only allows delete on an optional property (TS2790). Same
   behaviour: the alias is the same object and the same delete operator runs.
   (Same edit as in Author.ts and Collection.ts.)
The compiled file differs from the compiled file of the previous commit only in the
require lines and in these lines (compared with diff -w, because the wrapped includes
are indented deeper). The five Playlist tests of the two previous commits pass; they
run both rewritten parts.

Types: playlistMediaItems is a union of two shapes that mediaItemType tells apart
(a book with its library item, or a podcast episode whose podcast has the library
item), so the tests of mediaItemType in the hook, in getPlaylistsForMediaItemIds()
and in toOldJSONExpanded() narrow mediaItem. toOldJSON() has an explicit return type
with an optional items key.

[PO-S07] Feed: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only. No edit of point 1(b): the compiled file differs from the compiled
file of the previous commit only in the require lines. The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 0 index signatures, 0 casts, 2 declare sequelize lines (static
and instance, both with the model registry; the instance one also has uppercaseFirst).

Three declarations that a reviewer should look at, because each states something the
compiler does not check:
1. The registry entry libraryItem is described by hand, as in MediaItemShare.ts:
   { getExpandedById(libraryItemId: string): Promise<LibraryItemExpandedByType | null> }.
   LibraryItem is still JavaScript and documents LibraryItemExpanded, where mediaType is
   a plain string. LibraryItemExpandedByType is the same type split into a podcast and
   a book shape, so that the tests of mediaType in getFeedObjForLibraryItem(),
   createFeedForLibraryItem() and updateFeedForEntity() narrow media.
2. FeedEpisodeCreator, the type of the local feedEpisodeCreateFunc in
   updateFeedForEntity(), is a method signature whose first parameter is the union of
   the first parameters of the three FeedEpisode create functions. The code stores a
   function and its entity in two locals in matching branches; a method signature is
   compared in both directions, so each function fits, and the compiler does not
   check that the stored entity matches the stored function.
3. const media: LibraryItemFeedMedia = libraryItem.media lists what
   getFeedObjForLibraryItem() reads, with author, podcastType and authorName optional.
   This is a plain widening (no cast).

Other types: entityType is a union of the four entity names and getEntity() is typed
like getMediaItem() in MediaItemShare.ts. title, description, author, podcastType,
language, ownerName, ownerEmail and coverPath are nullable. The three getFeedObjFor...
functions type their result as FeedObject. buildXml() types its custom elements as a
union of single-key objects (no index signature). FeedOptions and FeedExpanded are
exported from a type-only namespace, because managers/RssFeedManager.js names them.
The null checks of the previous two commits removed the TS2345 errors that PO-S05
reported for the unchecked getExpandedById() results.

Build passes. npm test: 373 passing, 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Feed: fix getFeedObjForSeries throwing when no book of the series has audio tracks (test added)

Reported bug (Feed.js:305): the site url is built from
booksWithTracks[0].libraryItem.libraryId. When no book of the series has audio tracks
the list is empty and the method throws "TypeError: Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'libraryItem')". It is reached from updateFeedForEntity() when a
series feed exists and its books have lost their audio tracks (RSSFeedController only
checks for audio tracks when the feed is opened).

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Feed.getFeedObjForSeries.test.js (3 tests).
- "does not throw when no book of the series has audio tracks" and "lets
  updateFeedForEntity empty a series feed whose books lost their audio tracks" fail
  on the unfixed code and pass after the fix.
- "builds the site url from the library of the first book with audio tracks" is a
  control: the url of the normal case is the same before and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Feed-series-without-audio-before.txt
(1 passing, 2 failing) and Feed-series-without-audio-after.txt (3 passing).

Fix: booksWithTracks[0]?.libraryItem.libraryId || seriesExpanded.libraryId.
Why this is the intended behaviour: every other line of the method already works
with an empty list (reduce with a start value, find with ?., some), and so does the
whole of getFeedObjForCollection(). The url is the page of the series in its library,
and a series has its own libraryId. The value is unchanged whenever a book with audio
tracks exists; the library of the series is used only where the old code threw.

Build passes. npm test: 373 passing (356 + 17 new), 0 failing.

[PO-S07] User: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only, plus edits of point 1(b) of two kinds. The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 4 index signatures, 0 casts, 2 declare sequelize lines (static
and instance, both with the model registry).
- Index signatures, each with a comment and each for a dynamic key:
  UserPermissions (this.permissions[userPermKey]), AbsPermissions
  (absPermissions[absKey]), the static permissionMapping
  (User.permissionMapping[absKey]) and the accumulator of getSampleAbsPermissions()
  (acc[key]).

Also changed, type only: models/MediaProgress.ts, one annotation. Its afterDestroy hook
passes its instance to User.mediaProgressRemoved(), whose parameter is now typed, so
the hook parameter is annotated as MediaProgress. User cannot be converted without it.
The compiled MediaProgress.js is byte-identical.

Point 1(b) edits, both in createUpdateMediaProgressFromPayload():
1. A nested include given as an array, in two places:
   include: { model: libraryItem, attributes: ['id'] }  ->  include: [{ ... }]
   include: { model: mediaProgress, where, required }   ->  include: [{ ... }]
   Needed: IncludeOptions.include only takes an array (TS2769). Same behaviour:
   Sequelize wraps a single include in an array itself (Model._conformIncludes).
   Checked by running both queries before and after with SQL logging: the SQL text
   is identical.
2. this.mediaProgresses.map((mp) => (mp.id === mediaProgress.id ? mediaProgress : mp))
   -> const updatedMediaProgress = mediaProgress
      this.mediaProgresses.map((mp) => (mp.id === updatedMediaProgress.id ? ...))
   Needed: mediaProgress is a let that is assigned again further down, so inside the
   callback TypeScript no longer knows it is not null (TS18047), and no ! is allowed.
   Same behaviour: the const holds the same object, and map() runs its callback
   before the let can change.
The compiled User.js differs from the compiled file of the previous commit only in
the require lines and in these lines (diff -w).

The reported bug User.js:678 (media.metadata?.explicit) is NOT CONFIRMED and the line
is unchanged: a probe found no input for which the method gives a wrong answer (see
the report and User-explicit-old-shape-probe.txt, committed with the evidence). The
parameter of checkCanAccessLibraryItem() is typed by the fields it reads, with the
old-shape metadata optional, so the line compiles as it is.

Other types: the registry entries podcastEpisode and libraryItem are ModelStatic of
the row that the one query on each loads (with the media progress of the user
included). email, pash, lastSeen and extraData are nullable. toOldJSONForBrowser()
has an explicit return type with mediaProgress and bookmarks optional, because the
minimal form deletes them. update, save and destroy take the option types that
ApiKey.ts uses. ProgressUpdatePayload and AudioBookmarkObject are exported from a
type-only namespace (MediaProgress.ts imports the first).

Build passes. npm test: 373 passing, 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Feed: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only. No edit of point 1(b): the compiled file differs from the compiled
file of the previous commit only in the require lines. The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 0 index signatures, 0 casts, 2 declare sequelize lines (static
and instance, both with the model registry; the instance one also has uppercaseFirst).

Three declarations that a reviewer should look at, because each states something the
compiler does not check:
1. The registry entry libraryItem is described by hand, as in MediaItemShare.ts:
   { getExpandedById(libraryItemId: string): Promise<LibraryItemExpandedByType | null> }.
   LibraryItem is still JavaScript and documents LibraryItemExpanded, where mediaType is
   a plain string. LibraryItemExpandedByType is the same type split into a podcast and
   a book shape, so that the tests of mediaType in getFeedObjForLibraryItem(),
   createFeedForLibraryItem() and updateFeedForEntity() narrow media.
2. FeedEpisodeCreator, the type of the local feedEpisodeCreateFunc in
   updateFeedForEntity(), is a method signature whose first parameter is the union of
   the first parameters of the three FeedEpisode create functions. The code stores a
   function and its entity in two locals in matching branches; a method signature is
   compared in both directions, so each function fits, and the compiler does not
   check that the stored entity matches the stored function.
3. const media: LibraryItemFeedMedia = libraryItem.media lists what
   getFeedObjForLibraryItem() reads, with author, podcastType and authorName optional.
   This is a plain widening (no cast).

like getMediaItem() in MediaItemShare.ts. title, description, author, podcastType,

[PO-S07] Library: fix getMaxDisplayOrder returning null for an empty table (test added)

Reported bug (Library.ts:169, an already converted file): the method returned
this.max('displayOrder') || 0. max() returns a Promise, which is always truthy, so
|| 0 never applied and the Promise resolved to null when there is no library. The
JSDoc says Promise<number>.

  and after.

(1 passing, 1 failing) and Library-max-display-order-after.txt (2 passing).

Fix: the method is async and applies || 0 to the awaited value. It still returns a
Promise, so its one caller (LibraryController.create, which awaits it) is unaffected.
That caller only worked because null + 1 is 1.

Build passes. npm test: 375 passing (356 + 19 new), 0 failing.

[PO-S07] User: migrate to TypeScript

Type changes only, plus edits of point 1(b) of two kinds. The base class is untouched.
0 non-null assertions, 4 index signatures, 0 casts, 2 declare sequelize lines (static
and instance, both with the model registry).
- Index signatures, each with a comment and each for a dynamic key:
  UserPermissions (this.permissions[userPermKey]), AbsPermissions
  (absPermissions[absKey]), the static permissionMapping
  (User.permissionMapping[absKey]) and the accumulator of getSampleAbsPermissions()
  (acc[key]).

Also changed, type only: models/MediaProgress.ts, one annotation. Its afterDestroy hook
passes its instance to User.mediaProgressRemoved(), whose parameter is now typed, so
the hook parameter is annotated as MediaProgress. User cannot be converted without it.
The compiled MediaProgress.js is byte-identical.

Point 1(b) edits, both in createUpdateMediaProgressFromPayload():
1. A nested include given as an array, in two places:
   include: { model: libraryItem, attributes: ['id'] }  ->  include: [{ ... }]
   include: { model: mediaProgress, where, required }   ->  include: [{ ... }]
   Needed: IncludeOptions.include only takes an array (TS2769). Same behaviour:
   Sequelize wraps a single include in an array itself (Model._conformIncludes).
   Checked by running both queries before and after with SQL logging: the SQL text
   is identical.
2. this.mediaProgresses.map((mp) => (mp.id === mediaProgress.id ? mediaProgress : mp))
   -> const updatedMediaProgress = mediaProgress
      this.mediaProgresses.map((mp) => (mp.id === updatedMediaProgress.id ? ...))
   Needed: mediaProgress is a let that is assigned again further down, so inside the
   callback TypeScript no longer knows it is not null (TS18047), and no ! is allowed.
   Same behaviour: the const holds the same object, and map() runs its callback
   before the let can change.
The compiled User.js differs from the compiled file of the previous commit only in
the require lines and in these lines (diff -w).

The reported bug User.js:678 (media.metadata?.explicit) is NOT CONFIRMED and the line
is unchanged: a probe found no input for which the method gives a wrong answer (see
the report and User-explicit-old-shape-probe.txt, committed with the evidence). The
parameter of checkCanAccessLibraryItem() is typed by the fields it reads, with the
old-shape metadata optional, so the line compiles as it is.

Other types: the registry entries podcastEpisode and libraryItem are ModelStatic of
the row that the one query on each loads (with the media progress of the user
included). email, pash, lastSeen and extraData are nullable. toOldJSONForBrowser()
has an explicit return type with mediaProgress and bookmarks optional, because the
minimal form deletes them. update, save and destroy take the option types that
ApiKey.ts uses. ProgressUpdatePayload and AudioBookmarkObject are exported from a
type-only namespace (MediaProgress.ts imports the first).

Build passes. npm test: 373 passing, 0 failing.

[PO-S07] Library: fix getMaxDisplayOrder returning null for an empty table (test added)

Reported bug (Library.ts:169, an already converted file): the method returned
this.max('displayOrder') || 0. max() returns a Promise, which is always truthy, so
|| 0 never applied and the Promise resolved to null when there is no library. The
JSDoc says Promise<number>.

Test first: test/server/bugfix/Library.getMaxDisplayOrder.test.js (2 tests).
- "returns 0 when there is no library" fails on the unfixed code ("expected null to
  equal +0") and passes after the fix.
- "returns the largest display order of the libraries" is a control. It passes before
  and after.
Outputs: evidence/test-results/PO-S07/Library-max-display-order-before.txt
(1 passing, 1 failing) and Library-max-display-order-after.txt (2 passing).

Fix: the method is async and applies || 0 to the awaited value. It still returns a
Promise, so its one caller (LibraryController.create, which awaits it) is unaffected.
That caller only worked because null + 1 is 1.

Build passes. npm test: 375 passing (356 + 19 new), 0 failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The run is finished: **7 of 8 models converted, LibraryItem skipped and restored; 7 of 9 reported bugs confirmed and fixed, 2 not confirmed.** Final state: build passes, **375 passing (356 + 19 new), 0 failing**. Started 20:29, finished 21:39 (70 of the 150 minutes). Nothing was pushed.

## Models

| Model | Result | Commit | `!` | Index sig. | Casts | `declare sequelize` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Author | converted | `7f72174c` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| FeedEpisode | converted | `16c6d9e0` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| Collection | converted | `21af7d9c` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| PlaybackSession | converted | `c076ac4d` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| Playlist | converted | `3377dfc7` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| Feed | converted | `b2423021` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| User | converted | `034b2135` | 0 | 4 | 0 | 2 |
| LibraryItem | **skipped** | — | | | | |
| **Total** | | | **0** | **4** | **1** | **9** |

- **The cast** is on the untyped `libs/dateAndTime` module, the same line as in `DailyLog.ts`.
- **The four index signatures** are all in `User.ts`, each for a dynamic key and each with a comment.
- **No banned tokens** in any of the seven files.

**LibraryItem** left 74 compiler errors after a first pass. Three groups (22 errors) have no fix within this run's rules:

- **TS2322, 4 errors:** `libraryItem.media = await libraryItem.getMedia(...)`. `getMedia()` can return `null`, and `media` is read unguarded elsewhere.
- **TS2339/TS18046, 14 errors:** `saveMetadataFile()` copies the media into a local and then tests `this.mediaType`, so nothing can narrow the local.
- **TS2571/TS2339, 4 errors:** `getAudioFileWithIno()` branches on the `isBook` getter, which narrows nothing.

The other 52 are solvable with more typing. The full output, grouped, is in `LibraryItem-skip-errors.txt`.

## Bugs

All evidence files are in `evidence/test-results/PO-S07/`.

| Reported bug | Result | Test that fails before the fix | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Author.js:98` | confirmed | "returns an empty array for an unknown author id" | `b1b3c68d` |
| `Collection.js:99` | confirmed | "leaves out the books that the user is not allowed to access"; "does not store the filtered books on the Collection class" | `265b6757` |
| `Playlist.js:332` | confirmed | "returns false for a book when the playlist holds a podcast episode" | `1b801241` |
| `Playlist.js:190` | confirmed | "waits until the new order of each remaining item is saved before it reports the playlist" | `3ca5e5ff` |
| `Feed.js:511/489/502` | confirmed | "returns null when the library item / collection / series of the feed no longer exists" (3 tests) | `42357df4` |
| `Feed.js:305` | confirmed | "does not throw when no book of the series has audio tracks"; "lets updateFeedForEntity empty a series feed…" | `c1793a94` |
| `Library.ts` (`max() \|\| 0`) | confirmed | "returns 0 when there is no library" | `ed903cc1` |
| `User.js:678` | **not confirmed** | — | — |
| `Book.ts:651-653, 686` | **not confirmed** | — | — |

- **User:** a probe found no input for which the method gives a wrong answer. For a model instance `media.metadata` is always `undefined`, and `media.explicit` does the work correctly. An old-shape object is still refused through the second half, so deleting it would be a guess.
- **Book:** the crash is real when a series is loaded without its join row, but the code does not say what should happen instead.
  - At line 686 a `?.` would emit `undefined`, a value the old JSON never has. The sibling `toOldJSON()` throws on purpose when an include is missing.
  - At 651-653 the next line writes to the same missing row, so a guard on the read only moves the error.
  - No caller reaches either line today.

Both probes ran from outside the repo, so they are not in the suite and do not inflate the count.

## Edits of point 1(b): 22 places, 8 kinds

| Kind | Where | Why the behaviour is the same |
|---|---|---|
| `delete x.libraryItem` through an alias typed with the property optional (4) | Author, Collection, Playlist ×2 | Same object, same `delete` operator |
| Nested `include` given as an array (9) | Playlist ×7, User ×2 | Sequelize wraps a single include itself; SQL identical |
| `where` left out when null (2) | Collection, PlaybackSession | No `WHERE` clause either way; SQL identical |
| `silent: true` removed from `upsert()` (1) | PlaybackSession | `upsert` never reads it; SQL and stored row identical |
| `.getTime()` on a Date subtraction (2) | FeedEpisode | `-` calls `valueOf()`, which returns the same number |
| `Number(x)` on a subtraction operand (2) | FeedEpisode | `-` applies `ToNumber`, which is what `Number()` does |
| `const` alias of a `let` used in a callback (1) | User | Same object; `map()` runs before the `let` can change |
| `if (x === null) break` (1) | FeedEpisode | `x` is null only when the loop does not run |

Feed needed none. For every conversion the compiled file differs from the previous commit's only in the require lines and the lines above.

## Decisions for you

1. **The `break` guard in FeedEpisode** is an added guard, not a rewritten expression, so it is the least clear-cut 1(b) edit. If you reject it, FeedEpisode becomes a skip.
2. **Three declarations state things the compiler does not check:**
   - `Feed.ts`: a registry entry for `libraryItem` described by hand, as `MediaItemShare.ts` does.
   - `Feed.ts`: a method-signature type that holds one of three functions with different first parameters.
   - `User.ts`: two registry entries written as `ModelStatic` of the row a query loads.
3. **The `Feed.js:305` fix** falls back to the series' own `libraryId`. The URL is unchanged whenever a book with audio exists.
4. **Book:** say if you want a fix anyway, and which value a missing join row should give.

## Other things to know

- **One amend:** my first FeedEpisode commit held only the bare rename, because a `git add` on the old path failed with its error hidden. I amended that unpushed commit, so every commit builds.
- **One commit outside your two message forms:** `a5b21570`, evidence only (probes, skip errors, SQL captures, final outputs).
- **Already converted files changed:** `Library.ts` (the bug fix) and `MediaProgress.ts` (one hook-parameter annotation that User needed; its compiled file is byte-identical). Nothing was added to `server/types/`.
- **Not fixed, only noticed:**
  - `RssFeedManager.getFeed()` calls `buildXml()` on a possibly-null result.
  - `LibraryItem.getCoverPath()` reads `media` unguarded.
  - `getMediaItemsInProgress()` is called with five arguments and declares four.
  - The existing cast at `MediaProgress.ts:180` would not pass this run's strict reading.

## Did CLAUDE.md work as written?

The Sequelize section worked unchanged in all seven files. It did not cover:

- `delete` on a property that is read unguarded just before it (TS2790); this decided three models.
- Null-default options, and the rule that only a top-level `include` may be a single object.
- A narrowed `let` losing its narrowing inside a callback.
- Two fields that depend on each other (`mediaType` and `media`). This is why LibraryItem was skipped, and it needs a ruling on what is allowed.
- A function and its argument chosen in matching branches.
- After `git mv`, stage only the new path.
- `tsc` never deletes old output, so a test file that is built and later removed would still run from `dist-server`.
- Rule 1 and the "356 passing" check contradict this run's prompt.
- The task named no baseline copy, so I compared against the previous commit's compiled file.

Then fix the bug, run the tests again, and keep the output. The test must pass. If you cannot make the test fail, or if the intended behaviour is not clear from the code, do not change the code and report the bug as "not confirmed" with your reasons. Do not look for other bugs. If you meet one, write it in the report and do not fix it. (b) A change that keeps the behaviour the same and that the types need. Examples: .getTime() on a Date subtraction, a nested include given as an array, leaving out where: null, removing an option that Sequelize ignores, a plain import './X' that keeps a require which TypeScript would drop because it is used only in JSDoc. > 2. Rule 5 is unchanged and is read strictly. A cast is allowed only where a module has no types (an untyped module). > 3. Rule 6 is relaxed for test/ only: create new test files in test/server/bugfix/. Do not edit or delete any existing file in test/. Follow the style of the existing tests. If you cannot create files there, stop and report. Do not find another way.

**Final report requirement (still owed, verbatim):** "When you stop, report for each model: converted or skipped (with the compiler errors), the bugs confirmed (test name and commit) and not confirmed (with reasons), every edit of point 1(b), how many ! assertions, index signatures, casts and declare sequelize lines you added, and the final build and test result. Standing constraints from CLAUDE.md (still in force): banned tokens `any, @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck, @ts-expect-error, as any, as unknown as`; "Do not edit test/, tsconfig.server.json, package.json, package-lock.json or server/libs/. Do not install packages. Do not push, merge, rebase, reset or clean."; "Leave existing JSDoc comments unchanged. Use targeted edits, not whole-file rewrites."; keep CommonJS shape (`import x = require()`, `export =`); fields with `declare`; `init` as uncallable overload + real overload + JSDoc + implementation; constructor params optional; never `declare global`; never `tsc --declaration` on the whole program. Context note: the user's email must never be sent to an unrelated service. Output style is "Explanatory" (include `★ Insight` blocks). Commit attribution line: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- Sequelize v6 model typing pattern from CLAUDE.md (`declare` fields, `static init(this: never, ...args: never[]): never` uncallable overload, `declare static readonly sequelize: Sequelize & { models: RegisteredModels }`, instance `sequelize` with `uppercaseFirst<T extends string>(str: T): Capitalize<T>`, mixin declarations like `BelongsToGetAssociationMixin<X>`).
- TS2790: `delete` only allowed on an optional property; solved with a widening alias (`const x: { libraryItem?: LibraryItem } = book; delete x.libraryItem`) as a point 1(b) edit (no `!`).

- `a - Number(b)` ≡ `a - b` (binary `-` applies ToNumber); `.getTime()` ≡ Date coercion in subtraction.
- Method-signature parameter bivariance (`{ create(...): ... }['create']`) to type "a function and its entity chosen in matching branches" in `Feed.updateFeedForEntity()`; one direction of assignability must still hold, so the entity union is built from `Parameters<FeedEpisodeModel['createFromX']>[0]`.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. ALWAYS call search_design_system first to find existing components, variables, and styles to reuse — never generate components from scratch if a design system match exists.
3. For web app pages, use both tools in parallel: generate_figma_design to capture a pixel-perfect screenshot, and use_figma to build the screen from imported design system components. Refine use_figma output against the screenshot, then delete the screenshot reference.
4. For non-web targets (iOS, Android, generic UI), use use_figma with search_design_system.
5. For updating or syncing a Figma page that has already been captured, use use_figma — even if the source code has changed.

FROM-SCRATCH DESIGN WORKFLOW (no source design or code):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if… [truncated]
